title: Observations table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Reactivity (9F); energy transfer by heating
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 29 (Observations table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 29: The reactivity series. To understand how metals can be placed in order of reactivity using their reactions

questions.q: Write the word equation for zinc and hydrochloric acid.
questions.a: zinc + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + hydrogen
questions.model: Metal + acid gives salt + hydrogen. The salt from hydrochloric acid is a chloride. So zinc chloride + hydrogen.

questions.q: Order from the table: copper, magnesium, zinc, iron.
questions.a: Magnesium, zinc, iron, copper (most to least reactive)

questions.q: Why is gold used for jewellery?
questions.a: It is very unreactive, so stays shiny

questions.q: Write observations and word equations for each metal in the demonstration and use them to place the four metals in order.
questions.a: Magnesium > zinc > iron > copper; equations for Mg, Zn, Fe with hydrochloric acid
questions.model: Teacher writes the magnesium row and equation on screen.

questions.q: Why is aluminium used for drinks cans even though it is quite reactive?
questions.a: A thin oxide layer forms on it and protects it from further reaction.

questions.q: Predict what happens when calcium is added to cold water.
questions.a: Fizzes steadily, making calcium hydroxide and hydrogen; the water turns cloudy.

questions.q: Big question: why is gold still shiny after 2000 years?
questions.a: It is very unreactive, so does not react with water or oxygen.
